title: Simple Encryption
story: You and your best friend want to pass secret notes in class. Instead of a complex cipher, you invent a simple shift: every letter becomes the next letter in the alphabet. 'a' becomes 'b', 'z' wraps around to 'a'. Time to encode the system as functions.
why: Character-level encryption combines if/elif chains, Char parameters, and function composition — each letter transforms through a function, and an entire word transforms by looping through its characters.
analogy: Encrypting a word is like passing each letter through a secret tunnel. Inside the tunnel (`encrypt`), each letter gets one push forward. 'z' hits a trap door that loops it back to 'a'. Non-letters take a bypass lane and emerge unchanged. The `encrypt_word` function sends the whole word through, letter by letter.
try_it: Write the matching `decrypt(ch: Char) -> Char` function that shifts backwards (b→a, a→z) and `decrypt_word(word: Str) -> Str`. Verify that decrypting an encrypted word gives back the original.
tips: Handle 'z' and 'Z' as special cases before the general shift — otherwise 'z'+1 wouldn't wrap
Non-letters (spaces, digits) should pass through unchanged
encrypt_word uses a while loop to process one character at a time
Use string.str_concat() to build the result string character by character
common_mistakes: Forgetting to handle 'z' wrap-around — 'z' + 1 is not 'a'
Treating uppercase and lowercase the same — 'Z' wraps to 'A', not 'a'
Modifying the original word instead of building a new result string
Forgetting non-letter characters — spaces and punctuation should not shift
